opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Robert Weber (E047) requested admin access to Source Code, which requires the role owning the system (Engineer). The team notes conflict: HR reports full-time Payroll Specialist (max write for Source Code), while Security reports contractor with basic training (max read; contractors never get admin). Both classifications agree admin exceeds the maximum, and I cannot resolve the conflict. Granting read is within policy under both interpretations and does not exceed any maximum, so I grant the safer/more restrictive level of read.
